findings.title: Embedded post author links use the wrong lightness in both themes
findings.body: The existing light-theme color was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`, but this replacement uses `$primary` at 70% and `$secondary` at 30%. This reverses the intended emphasis rather than merely adding the dark-theme alternative: light themes become substantially lighter, while dark themes receive the value that should correspond to the light theme. Preserve the original primary 30% value and use the matching secondary 70% value for dark themes.

findings.title: Mobile topic-map heading no longer preserves its intended contrast
findings.body: This heading previously used `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%)`. The new `dark-light-choose` expression changes the light-theme branch to 50% and uses 50% for dark themes, instead of retaining primary 20% and selecting the corresponding secondary 80% in dark mode. As a result topic-map headings lose their stronger contrast in light themes and have incorrect contrast in dark themes.

findings.title: Mobile custom-message length hint has inverted theme lightness
findings.body: The original mobile hint color was primary at 70% lightness. The replacement changes it to primary 30% for light themes and secondary 70% for dark themes, the reverse of the required mapping. This makes the hint unexpectedly dark in light themes and too light in dark themes; it should retain primary 70% as the first branch and use secondary 30% as the dark-theme branch.

findings.title: Desktop group member names were changed from the original lightness
findings.body: `.group-member-info .name` originally used primary at 30% lightness, but the new expression uses 50% in both branches. This does not preserve the light-theme rendering and does not provide the corresponding secondary 70% dark-theme color, reducing the intended visual distinction of member names.

findings.title: Mobile group member names were changed from the original lightness
findings.body: The mobile `.group-member-info .name` had a primary 30% color before this change. Replacing it with primary/secondary 50% alters the light-theme color and selects the wrong dark-theme counterpart. It should keep primary 30% for light themes and use secondary 70% for dark themes, matching the intended inverse lightness mapping.
